rv.q: "At the Wake of a Dead Drag Queen," which was first produced even before that, could really be something.
It’s as powerful as it is entertaining.
Don’t sleep on this Wake , because this Dead Drag Queen deserves to live on and warrants a big-screen adaptation one day.
In the Wake of a Dead Drag Queen is a funny yet devastating story that needs to be told now more than ever.
Above all, what makes this show outstanding is its costume design and makeup.
At The Wake blends both light hearted joy and seriousness into a heartfelt show.

cn.t: Critics praise Terry Guest's moving yet celebratory play about an Atlanta drag queen who dies of AIDS, with Guest's dazzling performance balancing laughs and tears in a timely tribute to drag, Blackness, and queer identity.
